Plot directions of movement in an ordination

Source: R/AllGenerics.R, R/plotDirection.R, R/zzz-mae.R
plotDirection.Rd

plotDirection() draws a rose diagram of the directions in which subjects move between consecutive samples in two components of a reduced dimension.

Usage

plotDirection(x, ...)

# S4 method for class 'SummarizedExperiment'
plotDirection(
  x,
  time.col,
  group,
  dimred,
  ncomponents = 2,
  bins = 16,
  facet.by = NULL,
  max.gap = NULL,
  ...
)

# S4 method for class 'MultiAssayExperiment'
plotDirection(x, ..., experiment = 1L)

Arguments

x

a SingleCellExperiment object, such as a TreeSummarizedExperiment.

...

additional arguments passed to geom_histogram.

time.col

Character scalar. Specifies the column from colData(x) that contains sampling times: numeric, Date, POSIXct or a factor of visits. Time differences, as in max.gap, are in days for Date and hours for POSIXct times.

group

Character scalar. Specifies the column from colData(x) that identifies subjects.

dimred

Character scalar. Specifies the reducedDim(x) to use.

ncomponents

Numeric scalar or vector. The two components of dimred: 2 for the first two, or two components by index or name. (Default: 2)

bins

Integer scalar. Number of direction sectors. (Default: 16)

facet.by

Character scalar. Specifies the column from colData(x) that splits the moves into panels. Each move takes the value of its later sample. (Default: NULL)

max.gap

Numeric scalar. Consecutive samples of a subject further apart than this, in time.col units, are not a move. For visits, NULL skips moves across visits without a sample; otherwise NULL counts all. (Default: NULL)

experiment

Character scalar or integer scalar. For a MultiAssayExperiment, the experiment to plot; its samples get the colData of x. (Default: 1L)

Value

A ggplot object.

Details

Angles are measured counterclockwise from the first component (east), so 90 degrees points along the second component. Moves of zero length have no direction and are left out. The radius is on a square-root scale, so that the area of a sector follows its number of moves.

Examples

# Directions in a PCoA of three bioreactors
data("minimalgut", package = "miaTime")
tse <- mia::transformAssay(minimalgut, method = "relabundance")
tse <- mia::addMDS(tse, assay.type = "relabundance", method = "bray",
    name = "PCoA")
plotDirection(tse, time.col = "Time.hr", group = "StudyIdentifier",
    dimred = "PCoA", facet.by = "StudyIdentifier")
